name: disposable-mail providers
aliases: disposable-mail providers as storage (mail.tm, guerrilla mail, 1secmail)

card.summary: a disposable inbox with a 40 MB quota, created and read over a keyless REST API

free_tier.stated: a disposable inbox with a 40 MB quota, created and read over a keyless REST API

per_object_cap.stated: 40 MB quota per inbox, reported by the account object

retention.stated: messages persist until the account is deleted; no expiry is stated

record.chaining: the verification-code sink, measured end to end: create an inbox with no key, let a service deliver over SMTP, read the message back over the API. The scarce link is the 40 MB quota and the single shared domain.

limits.value: no published rate limit; the API is undocumented beyond the Hydra index
40 MB quota per inbox, reported by the account object

identity_cost.detail: no key, no email verification and no card; measured by creating an account

record.reliability_note: one active domain; a domain change would invalidate every address a script had recorded

evidence.proved: 200, one active domain maxxspace.com (id 6aa6b995482bea6f4a97f585, isActive true), read with no key
201, a fresh account with quota 40000000, used 0, isDisabled false; no email verification and no card
200, a 360-character JWT for the new account
EHLO returned 250 and an SMTP message to the created address was accepted; sendmail returned no refusal
200, the message listed with its subject and sender, then GET /messages/{id} returned 200 with subject, from, a text part and an html part

record.notes: Four requests and one SMTP message proved the whole chain. 25 MiB per message against a 40 MB inbox is the practical ceiling, so one inbox holds one message.
record.interface_detail: /domains, /accounts, /token and /messages on api.mail.tm; SMTP delivery to in.mail.tm

card.provider: disposable-mail providers as storage (mail.tm, guerrilla mail, 1secmail)
card.summary: mail.tm API: free with no API key and no sign-up, limited to 8 queries per second per IP address; the per-account storage quota is not printed

record.provider: disposable-mail providers as storage (mail.tm, guerrilla mail, 1secmail)

free_tier.stated: mail.tm API: free with no API key and no sign-up, limited to 8 queries per second per IP address; the per-account storage quota is not printed
free_tier.notes: the API schema at https://api.mail.tm/docs.jsonld gives each Account an integer quota; its value is returned only for a created inbox account

retention.stated: mail.tm stores incoming messages for 7 days

limits.value: mail.tm stores incoming messages for 7 days

identity_cost.detail: mail.tm: no API key and no sign-up; an inbox account is created by one API request with an address and a password

record.reliability_note: api.mail.tm/domains answers HTTP 200 with one active receiving domain (fldubai.com, replacing maxxspace.com); api.guerrillamail.com answers HTTP 200 with a JSON session; www.1secmail.com fails TLS verification (certificate not valid for the hostname), so its API could not be read
record.confidence_note: mail.tm and Guerrilla Mail retention is read from their own pages; API reachability is probed; the mail.tm per-account quota value and the 1secmail API are unverified

evidence.proved: the mail.tm API allows 8 queries per second per IP address
evidence.quote: The general quota limit is 8 queries per second (QPS) per IP address.

evidence.proved: the mail.tm API is free with no API key, no sign-up and no paid tier
evidence.quote: Completely free. No API key, no signup, no paid tiers.

evidence.proved: the API schema gives each Account an integer quota property; its value is not printed
an inbox account is created by one API request
evidence.quote: Create a temporary email account with one request.

evidence.proved: the mail.tm API lists an active receiving domain

evidence.quote: We store messages for 7 days only. Sorry, we can't keep them indefinitely.

Guerrilla Mail emails expire after 60 minutes

record.notes: APIs tested on 2026-11-03 returned gateway errors. Endpoint api.mail.tm/domains returned HTTP 502, POST api.mail.tm/accounts returned HTTP 502 with 0 bytes, and api.guerrillamail.com/ajax.php?f=get_email_address failed.
record.binding_note: mail.tm stores incoming messages for 7 days, so held bytes do not persist; the per-account byte quota is an integer returned only for a created account and is unverified here
